newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to rule against French tax breaks for biofuels.
newsitem.headline: EU to rule against French tax breaks for biofuels.

text.p: The European Commission is set to rule next week against a French tax exemption for biofuels because it discriminates against other European products, a Commission official said on Wednesday.

The scheme provides for tax breaks for biofuels such as bioethanol produced from cereals, potatoes or beet sugar -- a move apparently in line with a 1992 Commission proposal to implement similar rules throughout the European Union.
But the proposal is deadlocked and the French scheme discriminates against other biofuels made in other EU countries.
"This is not about being anti-biofuels. It's about the measures being discriminatory," the official said.

The Commission, in June 1995, already said the French scheme had the effect of subsidising the biofuels' raw products originating in France. It also objected to the fact that the scheme only benefited products grown on set-aside land.

The 1992 proposal on reduced excise duties on motor fuels from agricultural sources aims to encourage the production of biofuels irrespective of the raw material used, the arrangements covering the land and national origin.

EU finance ministers have been blocked for years on the issue which, like all taxation proposals, requires a unanimous vote to be approved. France has the most developed biofuels industry. -- Amelia Torres, Brussels newsroom 322 2876841
